0 GHOSTS
A ghost census by Intervue

Are there more ghosts in a Haunted House or a Hiring Cycle?

We rang the haunted house. It picked up.

Has anyone seen the other person?

Indeed asked 500 US job seekers and 500 employers about going quiet during hiring.

77 in 100 candidates said yes.

76 in 100 recruiters said yes too.

Then came the awkward question: have you ever ghosted anyone?

28 in 100 candidates owned up. 73 in 100 recruiters did.

Meet the species of ghost.

Every ghost has an alibi.

The ghosts are multiplying: 18 in 100 in 2019, 28 in 2020.

Ghosters facing consequences went from 6 in 100 to 54.

In 2026, 66 in 100 job seekers saw a company go quiet. 34 went quiet on purpose.

Recruiters ghost more, about 2.6 to 1.

Our imaginary house starts with one ghost.

Then four flatmates turn up.

One job opening draws about 180 applicants.

So, more ghosts in a haunted house or a hiring cycle?

Which ghost are you?

Be honest. Your answer never leaves this page.

Source: Intervue

Where the numbers come from

  1. Indeed, employer and job seeker ghosting survey. 500 job seekers and 500 employers, US, 2020 data.
  2. Indeed, The Ghosting Guide. 4,000+ job seekers and about 900 employers, US, 2019.
  3. NumberBarn survey, reported by Allwork.Space. US job seekers, Sep 2026, 1,411 respondents.
  4. CareerPlug 2025 Recruiting Metrics Report. US small businesses, 10M+ applications.

73 in 100 recruiters: Indeed found 27% of employers had not ghosted a job seeker in the past year.

2.6 to 1 is 73 divided by 28, both from the 2020 survey.

Candidate species are estimates: the 28% who ghosted, times how they did it (48% stopped replying, 46% skipped an interview, 7% missed day one). People could pick more than one.

The house and its five tenants are fictional. Survey figures count people reporting an experience.

Every survey here is from the US. India's number is the one we want next.
